milestones.name: Cooked scene draws on adapters without indirect execution, selected from the capability record
milestones.bar: Where both paths run, the same correct scene, with exact production-direct parity against a diagnostic full-range indirect reference at matching partitions (M1.3); on the iOS simulator the cooked valley is as complete as on Mac through lifecycle and rotation, and continuous in every sampled pan frame (function only), the way shipped compatibility renderers such as Unreal's ES3.1 mobile path or Unity's GLES fallback draw the same content with less GPU-driven work. The indirect path on Mac and Chrome is untouched.

items.statement: The capability record captured from a real adapter carries its downlevel execution flags, SceneSurface lends them, and CookedAssets selects its draw path at every rebuild from that record alone: indirect only when adapter-read flags include INDIRECT_EXECUTION, direct otherwise. A record built without an adapter (capture_device) holds unknown downlevel facts and never selects indirect: the public FrameHost::new → attach_cooked_scene route draws through the direct path and creates no INDIRECT-usage buffer on any device. A diagnostic mask that clears INDIRECT_EXECUTION in a captured record is opt-in only and recorded whenever used.
items.ask: Read the diff. Is the cooked draw path chosen only from the record lent through SceneSurface, never from cfg(target_os), adapter or device name, backend, or a private adapter/device query? Can any record not built from an adapter report INDIRECT_EXECUTION, by default, assumption or provenance marker? Does a test build a host through FrameHost::new (capture_device), attach cooked content and prove the direct path is selected with no INDIRECT-usage buffer or indirect draw recorded, alongside the adapter-backed and masked-record arms? Do the Mac app, Chrome and iOS routes build their record with the adapter-backed capture? Is the diagnostic mask unreachable without explicit opt-in, applied to the record (not inside thrum-asset-gpu), and recorded in evidence when used? Do unit tests cover selection with the flag, without it, with unknown facts, and re-selection on a new device generation?

items.statement: On the direct path the contribution creates no INDIRECT-usage buffer, cull uniform, visible counter or readback, records no compute dispatch, and draws each placed mesh with one draw_indexed over its whole meshlet-ordered index range (base vertex 0, one instance) using the same pipeline, bindings, instance record and index buffer as the indirect path. Discarded frames, capture-without-history, motion-history flags, device-generation restaging, remote feeds, material promotion and Sun casters behave the same on both paths; CookedStats names the selected path and leaves visible_meshlets None on the direct path.
items.ask: Does ./dev check run the cooked GPU suite (examples/v1-game/tests/cooked_assets_gpu.rs) under both an adapter-backed record (built with capture, not FrameHost::new) and an indirect-masked record, with each arm asserting its selected path, cull-count assertions on the indirect arm and None-count assertions on the direct arm? Does the direct arm cover discard, capture-no-history, device replacement, remote feed, material promotion and casters, not only a happy-path draw? Is the motion-history flag maintained in a step both paths run, and does the direct path allocate nothing it does not use?

items.statement: On this Mac, with the same build and cooked store, production direct D (selected through the indirect-masked record) has byte-identical final submitted output to an opt-in diagnostic full-range indirect reference R: one whole-range indexed indirect command per placed mesh with independently derived and validated cooked-range/placement arguments, and the same shaders, pipelines, bindings, buffers, placement order and state. This holds for every existing view: valley noon pan at 0°, 18° and 36°; a low-sun valley view; and the diagnostic scene with its volume, mirrored node and edge-straddling mesh. The selected production meshlet-indirect arm I is also captured for every view. Same-arm reruns of D, R and I are byte-identical. A D-only negative control omitting a visibly covered placed mesh must fail exact D/R comparison while R stays unchanged, and restored D must match R exactly again. Each arm records source/binary/store identity, adapter facts, capability mask, actual selected path, diagnostic mode, command arguments and submitted-frame identity. I/D full images, unthresholded difference maps, changed-pixel counts and maximum channel deltas are retained and inspected for the same correct scene; cross-partition byte equality is not required. Differences must be assessed, with partition controls where attribution is uncertain; no geometry/culling discrepancy, visible quality failure or unclassified scene discrepancy may pass. No pixel threshold, ignored-edge mask, production shader change, production indirect change or selection change is permitted.
items.evidence: docs/evidence/render/cooked-draw/README.md: BLOCKED. Named paths command fails at noon valley yaw 0: 1,506 differing submitted pixels with exact same-path repeats. All-meshlet and single-full-range-indirect controls isolate draw partitioning; planner decision required. Item stays open.
items.inspect: For every named view, compare selected production meshlet indirect I with production direct D: whole frames and native-resolution crops, with unthresholded difference maps. Check terrain triangle edges, silhouettes and entering geometry; mirrored and edge-straddling meshes; material/texture detail; Sun lighting and shadows; and volume. Require complete, correctly placed geometry, matching materials/lighting/shadows and no visible cracks, holes or objectionable shading seams. Record the assessment of every residual class, using retain-all-meshlets and full-range-indirect controls where attribution is uncertain. Edge location alone is insufficient. The checkpoint's 1,506 pixels and delta 18 are observations, never acceptance thresholds.
items.ask: Does D exercise the real masked-record production direct encoder while I stays the unmodified selected meshlet path? Is R a separately labelled, opt-in probe reference using independent cooked ranges/placement records rather than copied D commands or pixels, with validated complete per-placement coverage, base vertex 0 and one instance? Are every view and all three exact same-arm repeats present? Does the D-only visibly missing-mesh control leave R and its arguments unchanged, fail exact comparison, and regain equality after restoration? Can any control leak into ordinary selection, production shaders, direct resources, indirect work/output, M1.4/M1.5 comparisons or M1.6 cost runs? Do full differences and inspection reject geometry/culling and visible shading defects without claiming the unverified derivative/ordering hypothesis as fact?

items.statement: The indirect path's output on this Mac is byte-identical before and after the change: the M1.3 views rendered by the recorded pre-change base (the main commit immediately before this milestone's first implementation commit, stored in docs/evidence/render/cooked-draw/BASE) and by the claimed commit, from one cooked store, with the indirect arm's visible-meshlet counts unchanged and a same-build rerun control.
items.check: python3 scripts/cooked_draw_parity.py indirect --base "$(cat docs/evidence/render/cooked-draw/BASE)" --target mac-metal --output tmp/cooked-draw/indirect-mac-$(date +%s)

items.statement: Chrome WebGPU's record reports INDIRECT_EXECUTION and selects the indirect path, and its cooked valley output through the T2 browser tap is byte-identical between the recorded base and the claimed commit at fixed times (pan 0°, 18°, 36° and a low-sun view), with a same-build rerun control, in one Chrome session on real hardware WebGPU.
items.check: python3 scripts/cooked_draw_parity.py indirect --base "$(cat docs/evidence/render/cooked-draw/BASE)" --target chrome-webgpu --output tmp/cooked-draw/indirect-chrome-$(date +%s)

items.statement: The indirect path's per-frame work is unchanged: the same dispatches, draw commands, buffer usages and per-frame queue writes as the base, and the G5 tripwires pass against their same-load history with the cooked_edit bench built on an adapter-backed record and recording that it selected the indirect path. Paired, order-alternated Mac runs of the valley record indirect versus masked-direct GPU forward and contribution time and render-thread encode time, with build, load class and order; no speed claim is made for either path and no simulator timing is recorded.
items.ask: Compare the indirect path's per-frame recording in the diff against the base: are dispatches, draws, queue writes and buffer usages identical? Are the paired direct/indirect figures recorded with their conditions, labelled for load, and free of any promotion or selection claim?

items.statement: On a fresh, owned iPhone 18 Pro / iOS 27.2 simulator with the console locked, the ordinary iOS route attaches the cooked valley through the game's existing content selection and, over at least ten seconds, records an adapter record without INDIRECT_EXECUTION, the direct path selected, a drawn cooked generation, advancing presented-frame and cooked submitted-frame counts throughout, and no wgpu validation or cooked loader errors. The documented command builds, cooks, installs, runs and cleans up, and fails rather than skipping on any missing simulator, tool, lock evidence, error, undrawn set or stalled counter.
items.ask: Is the route's cooked attach the existing attach_cooked_scene selection, with the route unchanged when THRUM_ASSET_STORE and THRUM_SCENE are unset? Do the retained state records name the simulated model, runtime, host, adapter flags, selected path, drawn generation, lock state and source/content hashes? Is any OS grant requested?
items.evidence: Locked-console fresh iPhone 18 Pro / iOS 27.2: direct selected from flags without INDIRECT_EXECUTION, content generation 1 drawn on device generation 1, 12 advancing samples over at least 22 seconds, no cooked/validation errors. scripts/cooked_draw_ios_sim.py --lifecycle includes the ordinary function row; docs/evidence/render/cooked-draw/ios-function.json.gz and README.md.

items.statement: With cooked content attached on the simulator, a background/foreground cycle and the route's device-generation replacement each end with the cooked set drawn again through the direct path on the current generation, with presented and cooked submitted-frame counts advancing again, no background submission, no old-generation publication and no validation error.
items.ask: Do the state records after each lifecycle row show the new generation, the re-selected direct path and the drawn set, and do the route's existing witness counters show zero background or lost-queue submissions?
items.evidence: Same final build: background hold leaves presented/cooked counters and generation unchanged; foreground resumes; injected loss replaces generation 1 with 2, cooked_drawn remains content 1 and cooked_device_generation becomes Some(2), counters resume, lost_empty_submits/recover_failed are zero, no cooked/validation errors. docs/evidence/render/cooked-draw/ios-function.json.gz and README.md. Rotation and full visual/pan acceptance remain open.

items.statement: With cooked content attached on the simulator, the route's portrait → landscape → portrait rotation row (the existing XCUITest orientation gesture in examples/v1-game-ios/ios/route.py) presents at each new current extent on the same process, window, lease and device generation, with the cooked set still drawn through the direct path, cooked submitted frames advancing after each transition, and no validation error.
items.ask: Do the state records before and after each orientation show the presented extent, surface epoch, unchanged process/generation, selected path, drawn set and advancing cooked submitted frames? If the XCUITest gesture needed an unlocked console or an OS grant, is that reason recorded for this row alone, with the locked engine-state rows (M1.7, M1.8) proved separately?

items.statement: The cooked valley reads as complete, textured, lit and shadowed on the simulator.
items.inspect: Native-size simctl screenshots of the valley start view, the 36° pan end, a low-sun view, the diagnostic scene, and the valley in landscape after rotation and back in portrait, each judged whole and in full-resolution crops of the frame edges, horizon and objects. Inspection list: (1) terrain complete to the horizon and frame edges, with no missing patches, meshlet-shaped gaps, cracks or holes; (2) terrain reads as textured ground with its base colour, not default white, black or magenta, and no channel swap; (3) sphere reads metallic with sky reflection, rock matte, both facing outward; the mirrored diagnostic node faces and lights like its plain twin; (4) Sun direction and sky ambient read the same as the Mac indirect capture of that view (content presence only, not an image target); (5) sphere and rock cast Sun shadows onto the terrain; (6) the diagnostic volume is present and not clipped or blacked out; (7) after each rotation the image fills the new extent with the scene at the correct aspect, not stretched, letterboxed by stale content or missing cooked meshes; (8) no z-fighting, flicker or differences between two successive stills of a held view. Label simulator function only.

items.statement: Within its recorded sampling, the route's camera pan on the simulator shows continuous cooked content: every sample is complete, terrain fills the frame edges as it enters view, and no sample shows popping, flicker or missing geometry. The evidence states the coverage (presented frames over the pan, samples and their times, holds and the largest gap between samples) and draws no conclusion about unsampled frames; proof over every submitted frame stays with T2-CAPTURE M2.
items.inspect: A frame sequence of the route's camera pan (simctl screenshots or a simctl recording decoded to frames) with its coverage record, including samples where terrain enters at each frame edge and the start and end holds. Judge content continuity in the sampled frames only, check that the stated conclusion stays within the recorded coverage, and never judge speed or cadence.

items.statement: The G5 decision, the maturity ledger and the evidence README record both draw paths, the selection rule, each target's actual adapter flags and selected path, the parity and cost results and their limits, and T2-CAPTURE M2's handoff; scratch is closed out under the storage rules.
items.ask: Do the G5 decision's meshlet section and capability inventory, maturity.json and docs/evidence/render/cooked-draw/README.md agree with the code and the evidence, keep implementation, correctness, visual and device status separate, and claim no speed or physical-device result? Is owned scratch under tmp/cooked-draw/ retired or recorded with its closeout condition?
